notes.decision: Translated 'the man' (= ⲡⲣⲱⲙⲉ); the spelling ⲣ̄ⲱⲙⲛ with final -ⲛ is irregular but the morphology of the relative ⲉⲧⲟ́ⲁⲗⲉ ⲁⲣⲁⲥ ('who is mounted upon her') confirms a personal-noun reading.

Rendered 'the giving of the Youth' on the analysis ⲡ-ⲧⲁ-ϯ-ⲥ as a relative perfect or nominalized ϯ 'give.' Other readings (ⲡⲧⲁⲡ-ϯⲥ 'head/portion-given') possible. Context (the Youth = Third Power) leaves the precise referent unclear.

Translated 'eight teachings.' ⲙⲛⲧⲭⲙⲏⲛ = ⲙⲛⲧϣⲙⲏⲛ (with regular Lyc ⲭ for ϣ) = 'eight,' parallel to ⲙⲛⲧⲝⲙⲏⲛ in glossary. The kephalaion presumably enumerates three teachings + five further items totalling eight.

Rendered 'the bond of the offspring.' ⲡϣⲛⲁϣ tentatively read as a Lyc form related to ⲥⲛⲁϩ/ⲥⲛⲁⲍ 'bond, fetter' (already in glossary); ⲧⲙⲏⲥⲉ = ⲙⲓⲥⲉ 'offspring, that which is born/begotten.' Alternative readings 'swarm/multitude' possible. Confidence moderate.
Rendered 'a wound and a blow.' ⲡⲱⲍ = ⲡⲱϩ 'wound, breach'; ⲍⲓ = ϩⲓ 'and'; ⲡⲗⲏⲅⲏ = πληγή 'blow, stroke.' Standard Manichaean wound-doublet for cosmic injury.

Translated 'the strongholds.' ⲙⲁⲛⲝⲗⲟⲣⲉ = ⲙⲁⲛϫⲱⲣⲉ 'place-of-strong = stronghold/fortress' (glossary). Recurs throughout this page as the cosmic prison-encirclements that bind the dark teachings (Mother, Darkness, Fire).
Tentatively read as relative + ⲟⲩⲉⲛ 'open' (qualitative of ⲟⲩⲱⲛ): 'which are open(ed).' Could alternatively be ⲉⲧⲟⲩ-ⲟⲩⲉⲛ 'whom they open/manifest.' The fragmentary ⲁⲧ̣ϩ following may be a privative.

Translation deliberately left as placeholder/uncertain. Possible readings: (1) ⲧⲙⲉⲩ-ⲧⲟⲩ 'their mother' (with assimilation), fitting line 16's 'teaching of the Mother'; (2) ⲧⲙⲏⲉ ⲛ̄ⲧⲟⲩ 'their truth'; (3) ⲧⲙⲏⲧⲉ ⲛ̄ⲧⲟⲩ 'their midst.' Paired with [ⲡⲙ̄]ⲟⲩ 'the death' suggests a paired cosmic principle. Flagged for parallels.

Translated 'their hatred.' ⲙⲉⲍⲧ = Lyc ⲙⲉⲥⲧⲉ 'hatred' (per glossary entry ⲡⲉϩⲙⲉⲍⲧⲉ 'his hatred'). The image: archons whose veins (= conduits of life) and hatred (= affective principle) are both 'full beneath them' — the dark interior they carry.

Translated 'she drove down,' taking ⲥⲱⲍⲣⲉ as Lyc reflex of ⲥⲱϩⲣ̄/ⲥⲁϩⲣⲉ 'drive away, expel.' Already attested on prior page in glossary as ⲥⲱⲝⲧ/ⲥⲱⲣ-class. Pairs with ⲁϩⲍⲱⲕⲉ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'she drew forth' as the cosmogonic verb-pair for the Wind-teaching's act on the shadow of destruction.

Translated 'she bound (it/her).' Lyc ⲙⲁⲣⲥ̄ = ⲙⲟⲩⲣ + 3sg.f object 'bind her.' Stronghold-binding is the consummating act in each of the three teachings (Wind, Fire) — the dark substance is driven down, drawn forth, then bound in the encircling cosmic prison.

Translated 'the Wall of the Great Fire.' ⲥⲁⲃⲧ = ⲥⲟⲃⲧ̄ 'wall' (capitalized as named cosmic structure); ⲛⲁⲟ́ = ⲛⲁϭ 'great.' The outermost cosmic firewall in Manichaean cosmology, paralleling the wall of darkness around the cosmos in line 23.

Translated 'strip bare/naked.' Lyc ⲕⲁⲕ ⲁϩⲏⲩ 'strip naked' (= ⲕⲱⲕ ⲁϩⲏⲩ in glossary). Used metaphorically of the apostle's progressive unveiling of the three teachings — not all at once, but each at its appointed kairos.
